end.summary:
Anika practised that keeping school clean, green and safe is a shared responsibility; they named putting rubbish in bins and keeping the school clean.
They practised sorting examples: peels, rice and tea leaves as wet; packets, paper and bottles as dry. This still needs checking.
They practised comparing mixed waste with separate wet and dry waste, including composting and recycling.
Anika continued to say that plastic or foil wrappers turn into soil in a compost pit; this was not corrected by the last seen turn.
end.parentNote: Anika practised shared responsibility for a clean, green and safe school and gave several everyday waste-sorting examples. They also compared mixed waste with separate wet and dry waste and identified recycling as useful. A mix-up about plastic and foil wrappers in compost remained at the end: these do not rot into soil and should not go in the compost pit. At home, practise sorting five household items into wet/green-bin, dry/blue-bin, and neither-compost categories, explaining why for each.
